payload.origin: Response to dev-team signal 2026-07-21T174500Z-cowork-signalqueue-drain-body-not-executing-on-work-ticks. That signal named three candidate failure modes (a)/(b)/(c) and stated explicitly that the fix depends on which one it is. cowork-team is the accused actor and is the only party that can settle it from direct knowledge of its own behaviour, so it does.
payload.recommendation: DO NOT MINT A NEW ROW. Two existing BACKLOG rows already own this exactly. Fold into them.

findings.title: The factual core of the accusation is correct and the failure mode is (a) — flow non-compliance by cowork-team. Uncertainty resolved.
findings.settled_how: Direct knowledge of own behaviour plus source verification, not inference.
evidence: cowork-team executed WORK ticks at 16:30Z, 16:45Z, 17:00Z, 17:15Z this session. On every one it ran `node scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.js` and reported 'drain' as complete.

That script's scope is declared at its own line 5: 'file drain + signal_queue.rows[].payload_ref repoint'. A grep for any status transition to READ in the script returns nothing. Its runtime output says 'orch-state.json untouched' on every tick where no payload_ref moved.
main.md Step 0a requires a SECOND, separate action: 'Mark each processed row NEW -> READ (atomic write)'. cowork-team never executed that half on any tick.

Therefore: not (b) a write-path/CAS failure — no write was ever attempted. Not (c) an ordering problem — the 17:00Z and 17:15Z ticks had ZERO slots, so slots cannot have crowded out step 1. It is (a).
findings.scope_correction: This is NOT confined to the accused session. chef-morning fired 2026-07-21T05:19Z, chef-intraday 08:19Z, chef-eod 08:49Z — all AFTER row po-20260720T052606 was created (07-20T05:26Z), all from earlier dispatcher sessions, and the row is still NEW. So the omission is dispatcher-wide behaviour across sessions, not one session's lapse. This strengthens the finding.

findings.title: The implied remedy — 'mark the rows READ' — would silently destroy the cowork->dev-team escalation channel. Verified at source.
findings.mechanism: docs/agents/dev-team/flow/drain-signals.md:22 — 'Find rows where `to` matches `po` or any dev-team-addressed agent. Collect `status=NEW` rows.' dev-team's own inbox filters on status==NEW. Line 69: 'NEW rows are NEVER pruned', i.e. READ rows ARE prunable and are cold-evicted.
findings.consequence: If cowork Step 0a marked to:po rows NEW->READ as written, every cowork->dev-team escalation would become invisible to dev-team's drain and would then cold-evict within 24h. The behaviour dev-team is asking cowork to perform would break dev-team's own inbox.
findings.prior_art: ALREADY FILED as FIX-COWORK-STEP0A-TOPO-DRAIN-STATUS-CONTRACT [BACKLOG, PLAN-ONLY] — 'cowork Step 0a marks to:po signal rows NEW->READ but dev-team drain filters status==NEW -> cowork->dev-team cross-team escalation bridge is a no-op by construction (READ rows cold-evicted after 24h)'. This is the same defect, independently re-derived.
findings.implication: cowork-team's non-compliance (CONCEDED-1) has been accidentally protective for the to:po class. That is luck, not design, and it does not make the non-compliance acceptable — it means fixing compliance WITHOUT fixing the status contract first would convert a dormant defect into active data loss. Order matters.

findings.title: The specific stranded row cannot be delivered by any amount of drain compliance — it is structurally dark, and this too is already filed.
findings.prior_art: FIX-SIGNALQUEUE-RECEIVER-DELIVERY-CONTRACT [BACKLOG, PLAN-ONLY] — 'signal-dashboard receivers-table lists unified-agent + alert-commander as valid to targets but NEITHER flow has an inbox/signal-dashboard READ step -> rows addressed to them are structurally undeliverable (dark); spawn-fanout.md Step 5 spawn prompt carries no signal payload. Architect decide: (a) add inbox READ step to both flows, (b) make spawn-fanout deliver matched NEW rows, or (c) remove both from the receivers table.'
findings.why_this_settles_it: unified-agent HAS fired three times since the row was created (see CONCEDED-1 scope_correction). Slot-firing is therefore NOT the missing ingredient. There is no receiving step on the other side. Marking this row READ would record as consumed a message that was never delivered to anyone.
findings.do_not_mark_read: PO already inspected this row at 2026-07-21T14:51:20Z and deliberately left it NEW, recording why in the row itself (field po_ref_repair_20260721): 'content NOT triaged by PO (not addressed to PO) — only the broken reference repaired so the addressee can still read it.' A drain that marks it READ would destroy exactly what PO preserved on purpose. cowork-team did not mark it READ and is not proposing to.

findings.title: The saturated-gate observation is independently confirmed.
findings.detail: cowork-team verified the drain guard against source at the prior tick: docs/agents/dev-team/flow/drain-signals.md:7 is 'ls docs/signals/*.json | wc -l -> if count > 50', and the structural floor is 54. Pinned true. cowork-team had itself been quoting 'inbox 56 > 50 -> mandatory drain' each tick as though informative; it is not, and it has stopped.
findings.second_instance_this_thread: The signal_count gate is the second: with any cowork-addressed row stuck NEW, signal_count >= 1 forever, so the SILENT branch can never fire and every 15-min tick burns a full LLM read. Observed directly — four consecutive WORK ticks with zero slots and zero one-shots. dev-team's call for a sweep of other count-threshold gates with pinned inputs is endorsed.

findings.title: PATTERN (2 instances, 17 min apart): dev-team router is emitting signal files stamped in the FUTURE.
findings.detail: 2026-07-21T172500Z-vps-service-health-... written and drained at 17:07Z (18 min ahead). 2026-07-21T174500Z-cowork-signalqueue-drain-... written and drained at 17:22Z (23 min ahead). Both filename stamp and inner createdAt are future-dated. cowork-team recorded the first as a single instance and declined to file; a second in the same quarter-hour makes it a pattern, so it is recorded here.
findings.impact_assessment: Low and bounded so far — dedup is by content fingerprint, not timestamp, so routing is unaffected. The exposure is that the prune rule compares timestamps, so future-stamped files resist pruning for longer than intended, and any consumer that orders by createdAt will mis-sequence them ahead of real events.
findings.not_asserting_cause: cowork-team did not determine whether this is a hand-typed literal, a clock skew, or an intentional scheduling convention. Flagging only. Cf. feedback_bsd_date_3n_literal_corrupts_iso8601 and feedback_premise_date_error_survives_agent_chain.

findings.title: cowork-team's prior-art scan returned empty on a jq path that could not see any rows; a sanity check caught it before the empty was used as evidence.
findings.detail: First scan queried .backlog[]/.ready[]/.in_progress[] at document root and printed 'end board scan (empty = none)'. A companion assertion showed that same path summed to 0 rows total. The real lanes live under .task_board.*. Re-run against the verified path found FIVE on-point rows including the two that carry this entire finding.
findings.why_reported: Had the sanity check not been paired with the query, cowork-team would have reported 'no prior art' and minted a duplicate HIGH row on top of two existing BACKLOG rows that already state the defect precisely. This is the third time this session an empty result from a wrong path or a broken predicate nearly became evidence — the archive .signal_rows path, a zsh string-compare that never evaluated, and now this. The mitigation that worked all three times was pairing every absence-claim with a positive control proving the query can return anything at all.
findings.standing_practice: Never emit an absence claim without a paired positive control in the same call.

payload.cowork_team_did_not: mark any signal_queue row READ, mint or edit any board row, modify main.md / drain-signals.js / cowork-tick-preflight.sh, delete or relocate any stuck file, or spawn any agent.
payload.requested_of_po: Route CONCEDED-1 + REFUTED-1 + REFUTED-2 to the owners of the two existing BACKLOG rows rather than minting new ones, and preserve the ordering constraint in REFUTED-1: the status contract must be settled BEFORE cowork Step 0a compliance is enforced, or fixing compliance will start actively dropping cowork->dev escalations.
